cards.title: The screen
cards.text: Brawl Stars layout in landscape. Mark any part that's off.
cards.why: This is what your thumbs do every second, so it matters more than anything else on screen.

parts.title: Move stick
parts.text: Anywhere on the left half. It appears under your thumb.

parts.title: Fire stick
parts.text: Bottom right. Drag to see the aim line, release to fire. A quick tap fires at the nearest enemy you can see. Keep holding to keep firing.

parts.title: Summon stick
parts.text: Above-left of Fire. It fills as your hits land (like a Super) and slowly on its own. Drag to aim the throw, release to throw.

parts.title: Dash button
parts.text: Left of Fire. Tap to dash where you're moving, or drag to aim it. 2 charges, shown as dots.

parts.title: Top bar
parts.text: XP bar and level, the clock, pause (opens the build screen), and the minimap with the exit.

parts.title: Ammo bars
parts.text: Three bars under you that reload one at a time.

cards.title: How firing works
cards.text: Twin-stick aim, but survivor games usually fire by themselves. Which?
cards.why: Brawl Stars fires on release; Vampire Survivors fires by itself. Manual aim makes Bounce and Pierce feel earned.

options.label: Release + hold
options.text: Release fires, keep holding to repeat, tap = nearest. My pick.

options.label: Auto-fire
options.text: Fires at the nearest enemy by itself; the stick only steers it.

options.label: Release only
options.text: One shot per release, like Brawl Stars exactly.

options.label: Both, a setting
options.text: Release + hold by default, auto-fire as an option.

cards.title: Ammo bars
cards.text: Every weapon shape uses 3 ammo bars that reload, like Brawl Stars?
cards.why: It gives a bolt, a beam and a bomb the same rhythm on the Fire stick, and makes Haste and +1 ammo upgrades mean something. Without it, every shape needs its own rate rule.
cards.pick: Yes, 3 bars. A beam drains a bar per second while held.

cards.title: No aim assist
cards.text: Keep the maze roguelike's rule: no aim assist, apart from tap-to-nearest?
cards.why: Home and Follow modules already help aim. More help would make them pointless.
